source_caption:
Sean Penn as Colonel Lockjaw is funny one second, downright terrifying the next in Paul Thomas Anderson's One Battle After Another (2025). In that interrogation beat where he blurts the absurd line about being “raped in reverse,” you don’t know whether to laugh, recoil, or rewind it again. The scene works because Penn leans into absurdity with total seriousness, and the actors around him react like they’re surviving a real interaction rather than performing one.

Penn delivers his best work in years as Col. Steven J. Lockjaw, a rigid military officer who walks with such an absurdly stiff gait that it's become one of the film's most talked-about details. Penn ensures Lockjaw is almost subhuman through both his despicable actions and his physical presence, moving with a stilted, robotic motion while styling his ridiculous haircut with his own saliva on a plastic comb.

The performance threads the needle between menacing villainy and bonkers comedy, playing the virulently racist colonel as a painfully stiff, utterly clueless weirdo who believes he's the Terminator but actually moves through the world with the haplessness of Wile E. Coyote. Oscar buzz for a potential third win is very real.

source_details.synopsis: One Battle After Another is a 2025 American action-comedy thriller film written, directed, and produced by Paul Thomas Anderson. Inspired by the 1990 novel Vineland by Thomas Pynchon, the film's ensemble cast includes Leonardo DiCaprio, Sean Penn, Benicio del Toro, Regina Hall, Teyana Taylor, and Chase Infiniti, in her film debut. The film follows a drug using washed-up former revolutionary who is thrust back into the conflict when an amoral tenacious counterterrorist agent resurfaces after sixteen years to bring them to justice to cover his past sins.
